items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: The transcript describes Sidney Catlett as 'Ben's dear friend' and details Catlett's actions to help Ben Webster. The interviewee (Cliff Leeman) is narrating this event involving two other people (Ben Webster and Sidney Catlett). There is no direct statement from Cliff Leeman indicating a personal r

ctx.x: Ben was sighting his rifle while cleaning it out of the fourth floor apartment in Harlem, in New York, and somebody noticed him and called the police, and they took Ben to Bellevue for evaluation. Sidney Catlett, Ben's dear friend, went down to get him out. The psychiatrist, a lady -- the psychiatrist was a lady, and she was buttered up by Sidney, telling her it was all a big mistake, and all about Ben's virtues. She called Ben in and asked him what in the world he was doing in the city with his sporting…

It took more sweetness on Catlett's part to get him released in his custody. So you see, whoever may study these tapes to further his career, must understand a musician can have his recreation and create beautiful sounds at the same time. I miss the sounds of and the playing with Ben Webster, may God watch over his merry soul in heaven, and to cap off the Ben Cassy saga, I would say that as we ride off BENGAZI
into the sunset, I'm an old cowhand from the Webster band! (Sings)
